It makes sense to stockpile essentials that are easy to store and that you like personally. It's obviously not fun if you have a bunch of stuff stored that you don't really want to eat when the time comes.

I'm thinking of the following (as they come to mind, not in any particular order):

* White Rice (easy to prepare, no expiration date?)

* Camp stove with extra bottles of fuel

* Pots, pans, dishes and utensils (if you don't already have that stuff)

* Water in bottles

* Water purification tablets

* Campbell's soup and a can-opener (or pocket knife) - Avoid tomato soup because it doesn't store as long

* Common medicines like Advil, Tylenol, Neosporin, allergy medicine, etc.

* Sleeping medication and/or earplugs

* Hygiene items: toilet paper, surgical-type gloves, toothbrush, toothpaste, dental floss, q-tips, soap

* Warm clothing and sleeping materials

* Flashlight(s) with sufficient supply of fresh batteries (strap-on headlamp would be good because it allows you to work with your hands and still have light)

* Butane cigarette lighters (may be useful)

* First-Aid items, esp. Band-Aids

* Paper towels

* 1 or more 5-gallon buckets with lid(s) (can be used to store this stuff, but useful as a toilet or for other purposes)

* Zip-Loc bags in a variety of sizes (many uses)

* Battery powered radio with supply of batteries

* Pencil & paper

* Cash (small bills and coins) or other items you can use to barter

* Pocket knife or multi-tool

* Food enhancers like Sugar, Salt, Cocoa, and spices

* Working gloves (leather, or something sturdy)

* Sturdy shoes or boots

* Hat (for cold and/or hot weather, depending on your situation)

* Backpack to store this stuff or in case you need to bug-out

* Hard candy

* Books, toys, puzzles or something to keep you and/or your kids occupied

* Contact information and addresses for friends or relatives who you want to help or who can help you. Printed photos may be useful as well.

* Key information like bank accounts, investments, deeds, wills, titles, etc

* Barter items: ammo, cigarettes, alcohol (not for personal use, but because it might be easy to trade)

* Towels, wash cloths, rags (if you don't already have)

* Ropes, paracord, string and tape
